newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Thursday on profit-taking, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 3,392 yuan ($409) per tonne, losing 10 yuan. It opened at 3,400 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 3,430 yuan and a low of 3,390 yuan.
July fell nine yuan to 3,400, September rose five to 3,415, November was unchanged at 3,420 yuan.
Combined volume rose to 12,300 tonnes from 7,200.
Soybeans opened little changed but profit-taking pushed the two major contracts down for the rest of the session.

Traders said the poor performance of soybeans on the Dalian Commodity Exchange had hurt the confidence of long position holders in Shanghai, resulting in significant profit-taking in the May and July contracts.
"Investors are disappointed with the performance of soybeans on other futures market today, so a lot of them cashed in their positions," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in a narrow range with most investors waiting for some market-moving news before deciding what direction to take.
